questions.stem: Where does nuclear fusion occur naturally?
questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion occurs naturally in the cores of stars, where the extreme temperature (around 15 million degrees Celsius in the Sun's core) and pressure provide the conditions needed for hydrogen nuclei to fuse into helium, releasing enormous amounts of energy.

questions.stem: What is the main reason fusion power has not yet been achieved commercially on Earth?

options.text: Fusion produces too much radioactive waste
It is impossible to sustain the extremely high temperatures and pressures needed
There is not enough hydrogen available as fuel
Fusion reactions produce less energy than they consume

questions.explanation: The main challenge is sustaining the extreme conditions needed for fusion: temperatures of over 100 million degrees Celsius and sufficient confinement pressure. At these temperatures, matter becomes plasma and no physical container can hold it. Scientists are developing magnetic confinement (tokamak) and laser-driven approaches, but a self-sustaining commercial reactor has not yet been achieved.
